subject: SRE sign-off: Auto-rollback (SLO breach) alerting + oncall readiness for prod enablement
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: 
Date: Thu, Feb 12, 2026 at 9:14 AM PST
Subject: SRE sign-off: Auto-rollback (SLO breach) alerting + oncall readiness for prod enablement

Marissa / Connor,

Before we flip auto-rollback on for any production routes (even internal), SRE needs to sign off on paging rules + dashboards + runbook completeness.

Can you confirm we’re green (or what’s still blocked) on the checklist below?

1) Alerting & paging rules
- We should NOT page on every auto-rollback event (too noisy). Expectation is: Slack notification for all auto-actions, page only on “action failed” or “safety mechanism unhealthy.”
- Page scenarios (PagerDuty):
  a) rollback_executor errors / rollback did not complete within X mins
  b) monitor adapter failures > threshold (missing/stale/permission errors) that would block safety rails
  c) controller flapping protection triggered repeatedly (indicates config / telemetry instability)
- Notify-only (Slack) scenarios:
  a) auto-rollback triggered successfully
  b) auto-pause triggered
  c) rollback suppressed (with reason)

2) Dashboards
- Grafana: “Auto-rollback events” overview (by service/route/region/model version)
- Panel(s) for: monitor freshness, evaluation outcomes (fast/slow burn), decision breakdown (pause vs rollback vs suppress), and rollback execution latency
- Links from incident-bot messages should land on the exact scoped dashboard (rollout_id + service + region pre-filtered)

3) Runbook
- Triage flow: verify monitor validity + staleness, confirm decision rationale, identify culprit rollout step/model version
- How to override/suppress w/ justification, and how to safely re-attempt rollout
- Explicit “fail-open vs fail-closed” behavior documented for missing monitors

4) Enablement criteria (what has to be true to enable prod)
- Required monitors present for the rollout scope (no “best effort”)
- Labels/metric naming aligned with the standard (cardinality safe)
- Oncall routing: service owner vs platform oncall (clarify who gets paged)
- Staged enablement plan has backout criteria

If you can reply with current status + links, I’ll provide SRE sign-off (or a short list of conditions).

Thanks,
Sean

—
Sean Gallagher
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference

Marissa

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Feb 12, 2026 at 10:27 AM PST
Subject: Re: SRE sign-off: Auto-rollback (SLO breach) alerting + oncall readiness for prod enablement

Adding release details.

Staged enablement / backout
- Feature flag default OFF in prod.
- Phase 0: dev + staging only (already running).
- Phase 1: prod internal canary route only (1 region, 1 route). Enable “pause-only” policy first.
- Phase 2: expand to rollback enabled for internal canary once we have 24h clean monitor freshness + no evaluation flapping.
- Phase 3: service-owner opt-in for other internal routes; external customer tier gated.

Backout criteria
- Any page due to rollback execution failure OR monitor adapter errors sustained > 10m => flip flag OFF and revert to manual mitigation.
- Unexpected rollback volume spikes (beyond expected test events) => flag OFF and investigate policy configs.

Ownership / paging
- Primary oncall: platform oncall (rollout controller / control plane)
- Secondary (FYI/notify): service owner channel for the impacted route

I’ll update the release checklist with the explicit “no page on successful rollback” rule and the exact paging triggers you outlined.

Connor

—
Connor O’Brien
Release Engineering
Redwood Inference

This is close. SRE sign-off is conditional on the following being true before Phase 1 prod enablement:

A) Runbook finalization
- Confluence runbook must explicitly document behavior for:
  - Missing monitors at rollout start (should block enabling auto-actions; don’t “assume healthy”)
  - Stale monitor data during rollout (policy: suppress auto-action and alert notify-only; page only if prolonged / widespread)
  - Manual override/suppression procedure incl. “who is allowed” and required justification text

B) Alert routing sanity
- Confirm PagerDuty integration for the page-level alerts in PR-913 routes to Platform Oncall, not Service Oncall.
- Confirm alert grouping so we don’t page-storm on many rollout_ids (group by service/route/region; include rollout_id in annotations).

C) Dashboard access
- INT-8891 (dashboard access) needs to be resolved for oncall group. If oncall can’t open the dashboard link from incident-bot, it’s not ready.

D) Enablement gate
- Add a hard gate in the staged enablement checklist: “required SLO monitors exist + freshness OK” for the scoped rollout (route/model_version/region/tier).

If you can reply once A-D are checked (links + who verified), I’m comfortable calling this SRE-approved for Phase 1.

Sean
